defs: the time an employee works between saying they are leaving and the last day

items.situation: Mark asks: "Is the credit analyst in Brazil a new position?"
tips: No, it is a replacement. She resigned, and we replace her like for like.

items.situation: He asks if that replacement changes the budget.
tips: No. It is a budgeted position, so it is within budget.

items.situation: He asks about the two new analysts in collections.
tips: Those are incremental headcount. They are a net increase in cost.
incremental = more people than in the plan.

items.situation: He asks why so many people left this year.
tips: Attrition is high in collections. The market pays more for analysts.
attrition is singular: attrition IS high.

items.situation: He asks when the fleet controller leaves.
tips: She resigned last week, and her notice period is thirty days.

items.situation: He asks how the work continues.
tips: We plan a two-week handover. She hands over the cases before her last day.

listenings.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Every year we have the same confusion in the budget review, so let me be clear today. A replacement and a new position look the same on a requisition, but they are very different for the budget. When somebody resigns, the position is already in the plan. It is a budgeted position, so if you replace like for like, same role and same level, you stay within budget. If the manager wants a more senior person, it is not like for like anymore, and the difference in salary is a cost impact. A new position is incremental headcount. It is a net increase, and it needs a business case. One more point: attrition in collections is high this year, so expect more replacements there, not more new positions.

Hi Camila, it's Rafael again, from the rental company. Good news first: the committee approved the backfill for the fleet controller. Thank you for that. Now, the details. Her resignation is official, and her notice period ends on the thirtieth. I want a proper handover, at least two weeks, so the new person needs to start two weeks before she leaves. For those two weeks we pay two people, but only on a temporary basis. Is that still within budget? And there is something else. My operations supervisor steps down in June, and I want an analyst from the team to take over his job. Then I need to replace the analyst. Can we talk about how to classify that? Call me when you can.
